children: Shares in North West rose Wednesday morning after the Canadian grocer reported better than expected sales, driving profit higher in the second quarter.

North West, a grocer which focuses remote, rural, and northern communities, late Tuesday reported a 5.4% rise in second-quarter sales to C$682 million. This topped expectations of a more modest rise to C$661 million, according to a poll on FactSet.

The company cites strong same-store sales gains of 6.7%, as well as the positive impact of foreign exchange in its international operations. Last year, same-store sales were negatively affected by wildfire-related community evacuations in northern Canada.
Net earnings edged 1.9% higher to C$38.3 million, which on a per-share basis was a rise to C$0.76 from C$0.74 last year.
